Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can note that I was the passenger in the vehicle.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the collision happened?
A: It was in Pearland, Texas, at an intersection near a shopping center. It was a slow-moving situation, not a highway.
Q: How fast were you traveling when the impact occurred?
A: I'd guess we were going maybe 10 or 15 miles an hour. The driver had just started to pull out, and the other car
came toward us. It didn't feel like a big hit.
Q: Where were you seated, and were you wearing a seatbelt?
A: I was in the front passenger seat, and yes, my belt was on.
Q: Did you strike any part of the vehicle?
A: My head didn't hit anything. I felt my body jerk forward and then back against the seat. The belt caught me.
Q: When did you first notice pain or discomfort?
A: Right away I had a stiff feeling in my neck. By that evening my lower back was sore too. It has gotten a little wrose
over the last few days.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They said I had neck and back strain and gave me muscle
relaxers and some exercises to do at home.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries or treatment to your neck or back?
A: Nothing serious. I had some soreness years ago from lifting, but it went away with stretching and I didn't need a
doctor for it.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping and turning my head to check my blind spot when I drive. I'm following the
treatment plan and I'll keep my appointments.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
